Kitchen Operations.explanation: The campaign owner declares shifts (each with one role and slot count) and items in the menu. Adding a menu item generates its cooking steps via DishStepsService. Shifts, menu items and cooking steps are all composed by their parent, so deleting an item cascades its steps. Assigned volunteers complete each cooking step with a proof photo, or flag a quality failure, and log food-safety entries. computeEffectiveStatus decides whether a step is unlocked: the previous step must be done AND the scheduled time must have arrived - so the kitchen board cannot do steps out of order. Individual receivers issue a short-lived QR code; volunteers scan it at the distribution point to register the handoff. A unique constraint on (distribution, receiver) makes it impossible to double-scan the same person in the same distribution. Feedback is composed by the handoff, so each meal carries at most one rating.
